book.title: A Christmas Carol · Stave 3 — The Second of the Three Spirits
book.author: Charles Dickens, A Christmas Carol (1843)

cast.name: Ghost of Christmas Present
cast.role: second of the three spirits — abundance & joy
cast.canonical: a jolly cheerful bearded giant with dark brown curls, crowned with a holly wreath, wearing a deep-green fur-lined robe open at the chest, bearing a glowing torch shaped like a horn of plenty
cast.anchor: jolly bearded giant, holly-wreath crown, green fur robe, glowing horn-torch

cast.name: Scrooge
cast.role: protagonist — cold, miserly old man who is redeemed
cast.canonical: a bent thin elderly man with a sharp pointed nose, shrivelled frowning face, thin lips, clean-shaven, bald on top with short wispy grey side-hair
cast.anchor: bent thin bald clean-shaven old man, sharp pointed nose, hard frown

cast.name: Tiny Tim
cast.role: Bob Cratchit's frail, good little son

cast.name: Bob Cratchit

cast.name: Fred
cast.canonical: a handsome ruddy cheerful young man with side-whiskers and bright eyes, glowing with warmth, a scarf and a sprig of holly on his coat
cast.anchor: ruddy glowing young man, side-whiskers, holly sprig, warm laugh

panels.scene: a bent bald clean-shaven pointed-nose old man in a striped nightshirt, ALONE, sitting up in bed and peering toward a strange warm red glow spilling from the next room, all four corners open dark background
panels.composition: single subject — a light in the next room

teen.narration: THE BELL STRIKES ONE AGAIN — AND A STRANGE LIGHT GLOWS NEXT DOOR.

bubbles.text: It was his own room. There was no doubt about that. But it had undergone a surprising transformation.
But it had undergone a surprising transformation.

panels.scene: a jolly cheerful bearded giant with dark brown curls, ALONE, crowned with a holly wreath, in a deep-green fur-lined robe open at the chest, holding up a glowing horn-shaped torch, seated on a heap of Christmas food, the corners left open
panels.composition: single subject — the Ghost of Christmas Present revealed

teen.narration: THE SECOND SPIRIT — A JOLLY GIANT ON A THRONE OF PLENTY.

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: Come in! and know me better, man!

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: I am the Ghost of Christmas Present
Heaped up on the floor, to form a kind of throne, were turkeys, geese, game, poultry, brawn, great joints of meat
There sat a jolly Giant, glorious to see

panels.scene: the jolly holly-crowned bearded giant in the green fur robe, ALONE, laughing warmly with open arms, torch glowing, open background in the corners

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: You have never seen the like of me before!

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: Look upon me!
The Spirit stood beside sick beds, and they were cheerful

panels.scene: the holly-crowned giant, ALONE, striding over snowy London rooftops at dawn sprinkling glittering light from his horn-torch onto the chimneys below, open sky in the corners
panels.composition: single subject — blessing the city's Christmas

teen.narration: HE CARRIES SCROOGE OUT OVER THE CITY, BLESSING EVERY DINNER.

bubbles.text: the poulterers' shops were still half open
nearly closed, with perhaps two shutters down
a glorious pageant, with which it was next to impossible to believe

panels.scene: a bustling kind poor mother in a cheap gown turned and ribboned, ALONE, proudly setting a small roast goose on a modest table in a warm firelit kitchen, corners open

teen.narration: THEY VISIT THE HOME OF SCROOGE'S CLERK, BOB CRATCHIT.

bubbles.text: dressed out but poorly in a twice-turned gown, but brave in ribbons
Then up rose Mrs. Cratchit

panels.scene: a very small frail sweet-faced boy with big trusting eyes, ALONE, an iron brace on his little legs, leaning on a small wooden crutch by a warm fire, open background in the corners

teen.narration: BOB'S YOUNGEST — LITTLE TINY TIM, FRAIL BUT SWEET.

bubbles.text: as good as gold
he bore a little crutch, and had his limbs supported by an iron frame!
his active little crutch was heard upon the floor

panels.scene: the frail little boy on his small crutch, ALONE, gazing softly toward the window, tender expression, open corners

bubbles.text: He told me, coming home, that he hoped the people saw him in the church
he hoped the people saw him in the church, because he was a cripple
made lame beggars walk

panels.scene: a modest table close-up: a small roast goose and a round flaming Christmas pudding on a plate, warm firelight, no people, open corners

teen.narration: THE WHOLE FAMILY DELIGHTS IN THEIR SMALL, SPLENDID DINNER.

bubbles.text: there never was such a goose
nobody said or thought it was at all a small pudding for a large family
Oh, a wonderful pudding!

panels.scene: a thin poor clerk in a white comforter scarf, ALONE, raising a glass of hot punch with a warm proud smile at the head of his table, open corners

bubbles.speaker: BOB
bubbles.text: A Merry Christmas to us all, my dears. God bless us!
the greatest success achieved by Mrs. Cratchit since their marriage

panels.scene: the frail little crutch-boy, ALONE, lifting a tiny glass with a radiant sweet smile by the fire, open corners

bubbles.speaker: TINY TIM
bubbles.text: God bless us every one!
which all the family re-echoed
He sat very close to his father's side

panels.scene: a bent bald pointed-nose old man in a striped nightshirt, ALONE, leaning forward with unfamiliar anxious tenderness on his face, open corners

teen.narration: SCROOGE FEELS SOMETHING NEW — CONCERN FOR THE BOY.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: tell me if Tiny Tim will live

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Spirit... tell me if Tiny Tim will live.
with an interest he had never felt before

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: I see a vacant seat... in the poor chimney-corner, and a crutch without an owner

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: If these shadows remain unaltered by the Future, the child will die.
If he be like to die, he had better do it
the child will die

panels.scene: the holly-crowned giant, ALONE, turning a stern reproachful look outward, torch raised, open corners

teen.narration: THEN HE THROWS SCROOGE'S OWN CRUEL WORDS BACK AT HIM.

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: he had better do it, and decrease the surplus population

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: Man... if man you be in heart, not adamant
if man you be in heart, not adamant

bubbles.speaker: BOB
bubbles.text: the Founder of the Feast

bubbles.speaker: MRS CRATCHIT
bubbles.text: The Founder of the Feast indeed!

teen.narration: AT FRED'S PARTY, THE LAUGHTER IS WARM — EVEN ABOUT UNCLE SCROOGE.

bubbles.text: After it had passed away, they were ten times merrier than before

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: Ha, ha, ha!

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: He said that Christmas was a humbug

panels.scene: the holly-crowned giant, ALONE, visibly aged now with grey hair and a stooped weary frame, his torch guttering low, open corners
panels.composition: single subject — the Spirit grows old

teen.narration: AS THE NIGHT PASSES, THE SPIRIT GROWS OLD.

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: My life upon this globe... is very brief

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: It ends to-night.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Are spirits' lives so short?
Its hair was grey

panels.scene: two wretched, ragged, hollow-eyed starving children, a boy and a girl, huddled together clutching at a robe hem, frightening and pitiful, open corners

teen.narration: FROM UNDER HIS ROBE COME TWO STARVELING CHILDREN.

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: This boy is Ignorance. This girl is Want. Beware them both

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: Deny it!
where graceful youth should have filled their features out
Yellow, meagre, ragged, scowling, wolfish

panels.scene: the aged grey giant, ALONE, fading into darkness as a great clock begins to strike, throwing a last reproachful look outward, open corners
panels.composition: single subject — the Spirit vanishes at midnight

teen.narration: AND AS MIDNIGHT STRIKES, HE VANISHES.

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: Are there no prisons?

bubbles.speaker: PRESENT
bubbles.text: Are there no workhouses?
The bell struck twelve.
Scrooge looked about him for the Ghost, and saw it not.
